newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: S.Koreans lobby against Taiwan-N.Korea nuclear deal.
newsitem.headline: S.Koreans lobby against Taiwan-N.Korea nuclear deal.

text.p: Five South Korean lawmakers said on Thursday they would find it difficult to approve funding for the planned building of peaceful nuclear reactors for North Korea if it went ahead with a deal to store nuclear waste from Taiwan.

The group, who previously visited Washington, came to the United Nations to lobby against a deal signed last month under which the Taiwan Power Company is to send 60,000 barrels of nuclear waste to North Korea over a two-year period for a payment of $75 million.

Citing environmental and other hazards, South Korean National Assembly member Suh Sang-Mok told a news conference: "If this kind of deal goes through, it will create very bad public opinion in (South) Korea, which will put the National Assembly in a very difficult position to approve the government request for finance."

He was referring to a $4.5 billion deal under which a consortium that includes the United States, South Korea and Japan has promised to finance the building of two light-water reactors for North Korea, as well as interim supplies of fuel oil, in return for Pyongyang's pledge to freeze its suspected nuclear arms programme.
Light-water reactors are less suitable for producing weapons-grade plutonium.

Suh said North Korea intended to store the nuclear waste from Taiwan in an old mine about 30 miles (50 km) north of the demilitarized zone between North and South Korea. But he said North Korea did not have the required technology or experience to prevent serious environmental damage.

If the deal went through it would also create a bad precedent and violate the spirit of a convention intended to prevent poor nations from being exploited by richer nations as a dumping ground for dangerous waste products, he said.
